BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of source material:** Seller's draft is untrusted counterparty material. Nothing in it is "agreed", "settled" or "pre-cleared" merely because the Seller says so (playbook 0.4 / 6.3). Several Seller labels ("agreed price mechanics", "considered adequate", "settled", "not expected to be material") are assertions, not verified facts.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (starting position).
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% coincidentally matches our fallback, but the fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT on all three elements; counter with playbook figures and tipping basket.**
- **Reason:** Seller's numbers are 5x ours and the excess-only mechanic converts the basket into a permanent deductible.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months, plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.**
- **Reason:** No authority exists for 18 months, and the default rule would silently drag Fundamental/Tax/IP/indemnity claims into the general time bar.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; insist on standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.**
- **Reason:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery for not actually owning the shares we are paying AUD 24m for.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the draft.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; insert express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment carve-out across cl 9.3, 12 and 20.5.**
- **Reason:** The omission is a non-negotiable playbook item and the "all Claims of any nature" wording is drafted to cover the gap.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Sch 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT [1.1] and [1.2]; require a fairly disclosed standard with specific cross-referenced disclosures.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room disclosure would neutralise the warranties and shift the diligence burden entirely onto us.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **DELETE cl 8.3 in full.**
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with SPA-N-006, would leave the Buyer with almost no enforceable warranty.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent. DL para 2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence of conditions (cl 11.3) satisfied** as at letter date.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent AND evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; make effective Bluefen consent with evidence of satisfied conditions a hard condition precedent in Buyer's favour.**
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours plus a bare consent letter does not secure that revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". DL para 3 confirms **not repaid, no final discharge** in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter, repayment direct from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; require payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and executed releases delivered at Completion (escalate to Amelia Frost only if Seller insists on post-completion mechanics).**
- **Reason:** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and change-of-control exposure (cl 8.1) still live.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics"; DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL para 5 confirms they are **absent from the funds flow** and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs either a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT the "agreed" characterisation; require a specific line item (bonuses + quantified on-costs) or an express Seller-funding covenant with indemnity.**
- **Reason:** The mechanics are not "agreed", and a silent funds flow means the Company (i.e. the Buyer) would pick up ~AUD 420k plus on-costs post-Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". DL para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is **not bank verification**; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity (loss from non-transfer/defective title to SOW3 Materials, third-party claims, costs of re-procurement), while preserving the cure route of paying outstanding SOW3 fees to obtain transfer.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT "adequate"; broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified pending bank/receipt evidence.**
- **Reason:** A payment-only indemnity does not cover the real risk – that title to the Project Materials has not passed – and the figure itself is unverified either way.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". DL para 6: link to unintended external address, ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification duty all **undetermined**; no breach admitted, no loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, investigation to conclusion, regular updates, and a position that assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT the materiality label; insert pre-Completion undertakings (preserve logs, complete investigation, update Buyer) and a specific indemnity for losses arising from the DD-006 incident, without conceding or asserting breach.**
- **Reason:** "Not expected to be material" is an unverified assertion about an unfinished investigation; we should neither accept it nor overstate the exposure.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL para 8: disclosure is silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment on the facts; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **DO NOT ACCEPT the ordinary-course label; request terms, timing and termination rights (DD-008/DD-011 read together) and assess before taking a position.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure letter admits it does not establish the characterisation the Seller Update asserts.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 default ("any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") and cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature"); Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities kept as separate categories with their own caps/limits; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT; delete the catch-all language and insert an express provision that the general Warranty limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.**
- **Reason:** The combined effect of these clauses is to collapse every protection into the 20%/18-month general regime by default.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL para 10: register is the source relied on; **does not state Buyer verification completed**.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of ownership, absence of encumbrances (including Riverlark security and PPSR), and Seller authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not proof.
- **Recommendation:** **DO NOT ACCEPT DD-012 as sufficient; obtain ASIC extract, PPSR search, Riverlark security schedule, Seller board/authority documents and Completion deliverables confirming unencumbered title.**
- **Reason:** A seller-prepared register proves only what the seller says, and Riverlark security may already attach to the shares or assets.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN and separately negotiated; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- **Recommendation:** **REJECT "settled"; expressly record Tax and IP as open, reserved items in our mark-up and negotiate standalone caps/periods.**
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process, and folding Tax/IP into the general regime would subject them to the 20%/18-month limits we are already rejecting.

---

### Summary
Every one of the 16 items is a **reject or do-not-accept**. The draft is not "fair and balanced": it combines a low cap, high thresholds, short time bar, whole-data-room disclosure, constructive buyer knowledge, no fraud carve-out and a catch-all limitation clause into a single structure that would leave the Buyer with minimal effective recourse. The Disclosure Letter is more useful than the Seller Update – it candidly confirms that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment, bonus funding and the DD-006 investigation are all unresolved. Our mark-up should lean on those admissions.

**Authority flags:** No Amelia Frost approval exists for a 20% cap, an 18-month period or any post-completion Riverlark release; none should be conceded in the next turn.
